sources.title: Fugu beta announcement
sources.evidence: April 24,2026 names Fugu Ultra and opens external beta applications. English describes API access and two available variants; Japanese says external beta begins but describes a planned lineup. This is limited beta opening, not unrestricted general availability.

sources.title: Fugu general availability
sources.evidence: June 22,2026 explicitly makes Fugu and Ultra generally available, after a beta with close to 500 users. Original Ultra coordinates worker models for multi-step tasks; no exact parameter count is published.

sources.title: Sakana Fugu Technical Report, section 3.2
sources.evidence: Original Ultra starts from an unnamed pretrained language model and learns workflow construction with GRPO. Training permits up to five workflow steps; each specifies subtask, worker and communication access list. Agent tool trajectories are isolated within workflows, with shared history across workflows. No total/active count or exact neural backbone is disclosed.

sources.title: Original official integration catalog
sources.evidence: June 17 initial revision lists fugu-ultra, 1,000,000 context, text/image input, high reasoning, reasoning summaries and parallel tool calls. Client metadata establishes the interface profile, not public launch timing or a neural configuration.

sources.title: Current official versioned integration catalog
sources.evidence: Separately lists fugu-ultra-v1.0 with 1,000,000 context, text/image input, high/xhigh reasoning and parallel tools. Bare fugu-ultra is now displayed as v2.0, so that mutable entry is not used for original-version specifications.

sources.title: Sakana model identifiers and API contract
sources.evidence: Explicitly maps fugu-ultra-v1.0 to fugu-ultra-20260615, while the bare fugu-ultra alias currently defaults to v2.0. This identifies the June snapshot, not its release day. The current API provides text/function output and separate orchestration usage.

sources.title: Gemma 4 orchestrator validation
sources.evidence: August 10 technical note states earlier Fugu orchestrators were Qwen-based, without exact version or size. Gemma 4 E2B is a separate validation experiment; no exact original Ultra backbone or total is identified.

sources.title: Conductor research announcement
sources.evidence: April 27 post describes a 7B Conductor research model and identifies the work as foundational to Fugu. It does not say production Fugu Ultra has that size; the subsequent Ultra report describes an unnamed regular LM checkpoint.

sources.title: Fugu Ultra v1.1 update
sources.evidence: July 24 introduces v1.1 and explicitly compares it with v1.0, adding newer worker models. This confirms distinct revisions, without revealing original Ultra parameter counts or topology.

sources.title: Fugu Max and Ultra v2 release
sources.evidence: September 11 introduces separate Max and Ultra v2 revisions. Its updated pools and benchmarks cannot be transferred to original Ultra; no original parameter-count column is provided.

sources.title: Sakana API Platform Terms of Service
sources.evidence: September 28 terms retain service/configuration intellectual property with Sakana and licensors and grant limited permission to use the service. API rights do not license model-weight redistribution.

sources.title: Official Fugu repository inventory
sources.evidence: Complete 435-entry public tree contains integration code/configuration, demos and research material, with no model checkpoint. A SakanaAI HuggingFace search for fugu returned no models. These checks supplement the explicit commercial API distribution.

sources.title: Later multi-agent self-supervision research
sources.evidence: October 12 article describes a separate 27B research experiment. It does not identify that model as the production Ultra orchestrator or provide missing original Ultra counts.

name.note: Original named Ultra offering. Preserve its release history separately from the later v2 record; the current bare API alias is mutable.

developer.note: Sakana develops the learned orchestrator; worker models can come from other developers.

release_date.note: Earliest documented named-Ultra beta opening, limited to invited/applying testers. English says variants are available and Japanese announces external beta, while some wording is prospective. General availability followed June 22. The beta checkpoint is not explicitly equated to June v1.0;20260615 is a snapshot identifier, not independently verified release timing.

open_weights.note: Hosted commercial offering; no original Ultra checkpoint is distributed in the checked official public inventory. Public integration code and open worker models do not make the orchestrator open-weight.

license.note: Descriptive service classification, without transferring a worker license or the technical paper license to the complete model system.

parameters_b.note: No exact original Ultra orchestrator or combined-system total is disclosed. Research Conductor 7B, experimental Gemma 4 E2B and later MASS 27B are different models. Unspecified Qwen lineage cannot identify a production size.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-weight count or counting convention is disclosed. Workflow step count, selected workers and orchestration-token usage are not per-token active neural parameters.

architecture.note: Neural backbone topology remains undisclosed. The supported system structure is a learned language-model orchestrator emitting worker/subtask/access-list workflows, trained with GRPO; it is not a neural MoE merely because multiple independent worker models participate. Historical Qwen lineage does not identify a dense/MoE variant.

context_window.note: Official original June client configuration and explicitly versioned v1.0 entry agree on 1,000,000 tokens. This is interface capacity, not proof of native router/worker training context or an April beta limit.

modalities.note: Original and v1.0 interface metadata support text/image inputs; the composed service returns textual answers or function arguments. This does not establish an image encoder in the orchestrator itself.

reasoning.note: Original June interface supports high reasoning and summaries; explicit v1.0 metadata later supports high/xhigh. Reasoning capability describes the composed service, without assuming current v2 behavior.

tool_call.note: Original report explicitly implements model-selected agent function calls and their routing; both original and v1.0 catalogs support parallel tool calls.

description.value: Language-model orchestrator trained with reinforcement learning to compose multi-step workflows across a pool of worker models.
description.note: Specific to original Ultra workflow construction, including selected workers, subtasks and communication topology; avoids transferring the single-worker Fugu router or later v2 results.

patch.description: Language-model orchestrator trained with reinforcement learning to compose multi-step workflows across a pool of worker models.

sources.label: Sakana model identifiers and API contract
Sakana API Platform Terms of Service

patch.notes: April 24,2026 marks the named Fugu Ultra beta opening with application/invitation limits; June 22 was general availability. Exact beta-to-June checkpoint continuity is not documented. This record preserves the original release; current fugu-ultra defaults to v2.0, while original v1.0 is also known as fugu-ultra-20260615. The date inside that identifier does not establish release timing. Original June and explicitly versioned v1.0 metadata support 1,000,000 context, text/image inputs, reasoning and tools as service capabilities. Ultra learns worker/subtask/communication workflows with GRPO, isolating tool trajectories within each workflow and sharing history across workflows. Exact total/active counts and neural topology remain undisclosed; 7B Conductor research and Gemma 4 E2B experiments are not verified original Ultra sizes. No authenticated inference request was made.

summary: Corrects the unsupported June 15 date to the qualified April 24 named-Ultra beta opening, separates June 22 GA and original v1.0 evidence from the current mutable v2 alias, adds proprietary classification and replaces vague copy with documented workflow behavior. Confirms original interface capabilities. Counts and exact neural topology remain undisclosed after original training report and later primary research/revision checks.
